summary: Verified black-phone-screen fixes: (1) MinGW cross syntax-checks of NativeApi.cpp, DxgiCapture.cpp, MediaFoundationH264Encoder.cpp — all exit=0. (2) Ported C# ExtractSpsPps() line-by-line to Python and ran 11 test vectors (a-e as specified plus 6 adversarial bounds tests) — 11/11 pass, NO IndexError on empty/tiny/tail-startcode buffers. (3) Static review of SessionManager (Orientation route + StartStreamer + HandleOrientation), DisplayRotation.cs (DEVMODE/DISPLAY_DEVICE layout + constants), C#/Kotlin protocol symmetry, and Android manifest configChanges. All good — no blocking issues found.
critical_code_review_comments: ExtractSpsPps: NAL type mask 0x1F applied correctly; loop bounds (`i + 3 < d.Length`) plus explicit `if (i + sc >= d.Length) break` prevent IndexOutOfRange on any adversarial input (verified with 200 random buffers 0-64 bytes long, empty buffer, 1/2/3/4-byte buffers, and start-codes at the very tail). C# code matches the tested-good Python port line-for-line.

OnEncodedFrame prepend path is correct: cache updates whenever headers are present in the current frame; on a bare keyframe (no SPS/PPS in-band) the cached Annex-B SPS+PPS is prepended in front so a late-joining Android decoder sees SPS,PPS,IDR in order — this directly addresses the reported black-screen root cause.

DisplayRotation.cs DEVMODE layout matches Win32 display-DEVMODE: dmDeviceName[32] + 4x ushort (dmSpecVersion/dmDriverVersion/dmSize/dmDriverExtra) + dmFields uint + dmPositionX/Y int + dmDisplayOrientation/dmDisplayFixedOutput uint + 5x short + dmFormName[32] + dmLogPixels ushort + 5x uint (dmBitsPerPel..dmDisplayFrequency) + 8x uint (dmICMMethod..dmPanningHeight). Constants DM_PELSWIDTH=0x80000, DM_PELSHEIGHT=0x100000, DM_DISPLAYORIENTATION=0x80, DMDO_90=1/180=2/270=3 all correct.

SessionManager.Route has `case MessageType.Orientation: HandleOrientation(json)` at line 112; fields `_lastVideoCfg` (line 40) and `_lastRotation` (line 41) exist; StartStreamer helper (line 216) caches cfg; HandleOrientation (line 238) properly guards `!Diagnostics.UsingVirtualDisplay` (mirror mode is skipped), stops streamer, calls `DisplayRotation.SetRotation`, awaits 800ms, recomputes OutputIndex via `NativeSafeOutputCount()-1`, restarts streamer, and requests a keyframe.

Protocol symmetry OK: C# `MessageType.Orientation = "ORIENTATION"` (Protocol.cs:64), Kotlin `MessageType.ORIENTATION = "ORIENTATION"` (Protocol.kt:59), Android `ConnectionManager.sendOrientation` sends `{type:"ORIENTATION", rotation:<int>}` (lines 196-204), C# `OrientationMessage` has `[JsonPropertyName("rotation")]` (Messages.cs:114).

AndroidManifest MonitorActivity has `android:configChanges="orientation|screenSize|screenLayout|keyboardHidden|smallestScreenSize"` — onConfigurationChanged is guaranteed to fire on rotation without recreating the Activity, so the stream keeps running and sendOrientation() fires immediately.

H264Decoder keyframe input-buffer retry loop is correct (up to ~100ms) — protects against MediaCodec being briefly full when the SPS/PPS-carrying IDR arrives; `var inIndex` allowed to be reassigned in the retry loop.

VideoReceiver.packetsReceived++ correctly counts only well-formed packets (past magic/length checks); framesReassembled++ increments only on complete reassembly; both wired to overlay via VideoPipeline properties.

NativeApi WorkerLoop: `gdiOnly = g_capture.Rotated()` and `gdiIntervalMs = 33ms (~30fps)` correctly switch to GDI-only path when the desktop is rotated (DXGI Desktop Duplication returns unrotated frames for rotated outputs); `lastKeyframe` 1s cadence prevents keyframe spam.

Minor observation (not a bug): `_lastRotation = rot` in HandleOrientation is set BEFORE checking SetRotation success — if SetRotation fails the cached rotation drifts from reality. Low priority since the Android side will resend on next config change.

Minor observation (not a bug): `while (i + 3 < d.Length)` misses detection of a bare 3-byte startcode located at the exact last 3 bytes of the buffer, but that startcode would have no NAL body to extract anyway — safe no-op.
SwDevice.cpp still fails MinGW syntax check (missing swdevice.h) — expected/documented in iteration_1; not a regression.
